input_contract.window: valid locked DOS window id; high byte names a present window, low-byte object index is less than count
input_contract.object_geometry: accessible 8-byte signed Rect at the selected object-table far pointer, normalized in the bounded logical screen x=0..640,y=0..400
input_contract.memory: valid Ralloc-backed window/master table; output is the actual supplied far pointer

source_based_explanation: Pinned root:2505 source calls win_LockWin(obj), obtains the window with f_2505_0006(obj), selects the far Rect pointer at window+0x2C indexed by obj&0xFF, copies all four words through the supplied far pointer, then calls win_UnlockWin(obj).
The clip callback supplies only the indexed Rect for each valid window ID, records ordered calls, and writes through the actual far pointer passed by original f_1E57_038E.

A separate 100-case direct integration runs original win_GetObjRect with original lock/window lookup/unlock helpers over 1..6 object records; the 265-case clip suite runs original f_1D8E_02BD and original allocator/memory helpers.
input_domain: valid locked DOS window object id; high byte selects a present window and low-byte object index is less than object count
accessible 8-byte signed Rect at the selected object-table far pointer; normalized x=0..640,y=0..400
valid Ralloc-backed window/master table and actual supplied far output pointer
limitations: No malformed/unmapped object indices, inaccessible pointers, invalid handles, or arbitrary resource geometry.
The model supplies per-case window Rects; it does not reconstruct full window manager or resource loading behavior.
